title: Jean-François Lyotard
summary: French philosopher (1924–1998) who treated desire as an economy and later named the postmodern as incredulity toward grand narratives.
whyItMatters: Two books travel: Économie libidinale (1974) is the libidinal-economy move; The Postmodern Condition (1979) is why people say ‘metanarrative.’
notes: Not a system-builder. Read him for those two interventions, not for a complete theory of society. Économie libidinale is the libidinal-economy book.
